notes.title: Dev Update #002
notes.content:
[p]Welcome to our next Update. Today we want to tell you something about our thoughts about load and save mechanics.

[b]Flexible Save Points[/b][/p][p]In a role-playing game like the one we're aiming for, the ability to save multiple times in a computer game, regardless of where you are in the game, offers several advantages over fixed save points or checkpoints. When players are able to save at any point in the game, they have more flexibility and control over their progress.
This reduces frustration when reaching difficult situations or enemies that can be beaten in smaller steps, rather than having to repeat the entire section.

Furthermore, flexible save options allow you to try out different strategies or decisions without fear of consequences. Whether you accept every consequence or not is up to you.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514382/49ed409ac1a56fb99206fb933703ad5384a5468d.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Technical Challenges[/b][/p][p]However, such freedom also brings challenges, because we as developers have to be careful not to overload the storage capacity by creating files that are too large.

With the option to save everywhere, we have to make sure to be aware of various possible situations so that players don't "destroy" their savefiles. For example, if the player is almost out of life energy and is getting damage at the same time, saving should no longer be allowed, as the save file would be unusable. Implementing a flexible save function can be technically challenging, especially if the game has complex mechanics or large game worlds.

Also, the save function should not be used to avoid certain challenges or make them too easy.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514382/6bd60708151d916d48407939f7f61f536fcd2bab.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Solution[/b][/p][p]For this reason, for Cralon we decided to implement both a system of automatic save points as well as a limited selection of save slots that can be used manually. This way, you can always load and decide when to use save points, but on the other hand, you still have to think about the right time to save without using too much memory.[/p][p][/p][p]More about our thoughts and decisions can also be found on our Youtube Channel.[/p][p]Thank you for your interest, see you soon![/p][p]Jenny and Björn[/p]

notes.title: Dev Update #001
notes.content:
Hello and thank you for coming here. On our way to the release of our first game, we'd like to keep you updated with different news about the development here and on our Pithead Studio YouTube channel.

[b]First Person View[/b]

First of all, we'd like to tell you more about our ideas and thoughts regarding our decision for the first-person view.  The idea of ​​creating more immersion by seeing the game directly from the main character's perspective also allows features like inspecting objects to place more emphasis on exploring the environment.
One of our goals was to expand the game's existing role-playing elements with first-person adventure elements to make the environment more interesting during gameplay and encourage players to examine everything more closely, while also being rewarded for doing so.

[b]Making the Player Character Visible[/b]

There are various ways to represent first-person mode. In many games, for example, only the player character's hands, weapons or arms are visualized, but not the body. This clearly has the advantage of saving work and animations for the representation.
On the other hand it's better to be able to see your body when looking down on yourself, to create as much immersion as possible. We ultimately decided to actually represent the player character visually, including its movements and, of course, the chosen weapons, to enable a more immersive experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514382/1bc2f73bab5aad4f6bb2cc487454a6114dd4db1a.jpg[/img]

[b]Shadows[/b]

This decision has another positive aspect. If you place the main character in front of a light source, such as a lamp or torch, a shadow of your own silhouette is cast onto the wall or floor. This gives you the feeling of actually immersing yourself into the game world and isn't distracted or pulled out of the action by unrealistic visual simplifications.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514382/5cf74020d2acb9b61893a7d3e681643dbdfd193a.png[/img]

In order to be able to empathize with what it feels like to walk around in the shaft and be exposed to various, sometimes even scary, situations, it is important to us to implement features and new game elements as immersively as possible.

Thank you for your interest, see you soon!
Jenny and Björn

notes.title: Former Piranha Bytes veterans unveil their new dungeon crawler, and it's tripping my Arx Fatalis alarms in all the right ways
notes.content: Back in July 2024, former Piranha Bytes creative director Björn Pankratz and his wife, game designer Jennifer Pankratz, launched a new indie outfit called Pithead Studio, which they said would enable them to "keep doing what we love." Today we got our first look at what that is, and I am—with all appropriate caution engaged—very excited... Read more.

notes.title: Cralon Announcement!
notes.content:
Hi,

we are Jenny and Björn Pankratz and some of you may know us as two former visionary developers from the company behind the Gothic-, Risen- and ELEX-series.

Now we founded our own indie studio Pithead Studio and we are thrilled to announce our brand-new game Cralon.

Cralon is an authentic 3D dungeon crawler with RPG and adventure elements, inspired by the ultimate dungeon classics and developed with the Unreal Engine 5. It combines a variety of interlocking game elements that enhance the immersion of exploration and storytelling.

Check out the new announcement trailer, spread the word and wishlist, if you like it. We are looking forward to share more with you and hope you join us on our journey.

We are really happy to be back.

See you soon!
Jenny & Björn
